text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU pool pressure detected in aws-ap-northeast-1. Autoscaler attempted scale-up x3 but requests are in SUSPENDED state due to cloud limit (Account-level GPU vCPU quota). Queue growth observed on inference-queue-01. Severity: P2.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-GBP-782. Impact: increased 5xxs to downstream callers, tail latency > 3s for a subset of requests, 3 high-volume tenants showing elevated error rates.

matt_oncall: Ack. I'm on it. Assigning to infra + cloud eng.

lucy_infra: Looking at autoscaler logs — saw continuous failures to create node group: error from provider api: "Exceeded quota: GPUs". Autoscaler state: pendingScaleUp -> scaleHold.

jaya_cloud: Confirming with GCP console (account is our AWS Org): account-level GPU soft cap reached for p4d/p3 family in ap-northeast-1. We have some free GPUs in other AZs but not same AZ, and cross-AZ placement isn't allowed by current zoneAffinity policy.

alex_sre: Can we fallback to lower-spec instance types (g4dn/g5) for burst jobs? That may reduce perf but keep infra alive.

matt_oncall: Good idea. Lucy, how hard is it to add a fallback profile?

lucy_infra: We have a fallback pool config but it's disabled for this cluster. Enabling it requires a small rollout to the autoscaler policy. I can flip it to allow g5s, but need a quick config snippet.

lucy_infra: Pasting proposed k8s autoscaler patch:
```yaml
spec:
  scaleTargets:
    - pool: inference-gpu-primary
      allowedInstanceTypes: [p4d,p3,g5,g4dn]
  policy:
    zoneAffinity: soft
    fallback: true
```

jaya_cloud: Before we change, note that account quota for g5 is also near limit. Might buy us ~30% capacity but not full demand.

emily_prod_metrics: Metrics: request_queue_length for inference-queue-01 jumped from 40 -> 720 in last 9m. 95th latency for /v1/complete at 12s. Error rate increased from 0.2% -> 6.3% for tenant:acme-inc.

anya_support: Support: we're getting a drip of high-priority tickets for timeouts. I'll draft a short customer message once we confirm mitigation path.

matt_oncall: Priority order: 1) stop user-impacting 5xxs ASAP (mitigate), 2) keep system functional (throughput), 3) postmortem root cause.

alex_sre: Immediate mitigations we can do in parallel: 1) enable CPU fallback for low-priority queues (soft degrade model), 2) enable autoscaler fallback to g5/g4dn, 3) temporarily reject very large batch jobs with 429 to protect critical traffic.

lucy_infra: Starting autoscaler patch now. Will roll for 10s. ETA ~90s.

matt_oncall: I'll queue the throttling rule: add policy to routing layer to reject batches above 2048 tokens.

jaya_cloud: Opening support case with AWS account team for urgent quota increase. Case: 987654321. Requested +150 GPUs in ap-northeast-1. ETA from AWS pending (usually 1-3h).

incident-bot: Deploy check: autoscaler-policy v2.14 -> v2.15 in progress.

lucy_infra: Rollout succeeded on 6/6 nodes. Fallback allowed to g5/g4dn.

lucy_infra: Spinning up g5 nodes now. API shows pending capacity in ap-northeast-1, creating 6 g5.

emily_prod_metrics: Queue length dropping: 720 -> 210 over 3m. 95th latency down to 2.1s. Error rate for acme-inc down to 1.7%. Good trend.

anya_support: Draft customer message: "We're experiencing temporary GPU capacity pressure in ap-northeast-1 affecting a subset of requests. We've enabled degraded fallback to keep requests serving while we request additional capacity. Expect intermittent higher latencies for up to a few hours. We'll update as we have more info." Want review before sending.

matt_oncall: Looks fine. Send to impacted tenants list and paste into status.redwood.ai with incidents tag.

jaya_cloud: AWS case update: they acknowledged, escalated to account team. No hard ETA yet but prioritized.

alex_sre: Note: fallback to g5 reduces per-token throughput -> costs up ~12% per token for those requests. Logging to cost-anomaly so billing gets flagged.

lucy_infra: Observed one failing provisioning attempt flagged with "InsufficientInstanceCapacity" for p4d. That's why autoscaler kept failing earlier. g5 requests are succeeding so far.

matt_oncall: On-call handoff: I need to step away for 25m. @lucy_infra you'll continue monitoring? If load spikes again, escalate to oncall-backup.

lucy_infra: I'll monitor for next 30m and keep fallback enabled until quota confirmed increased.

emily_prod_metrics: Adding retention check: we'll watch model-quality signals to ensure fallback doesn't regress outputs beyond threshold. Current regression delta for top prompt sets is +2% which is acceptable for now.

anya_support: Message sent to impacted tenants and status page updated. Linking incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-GBP-782

jaya_cloud: Also changed autoscaler policy to allow cross-AZ placement for fallback pools — should help future bursts.

matt_oncall: Thanks all. Next steps: keep fallback until AWS/GCP quota bump confirmed. Postmortem will look at placement policies and proactive quota monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident status: MONITORING. Updated severity: P3.

lucy_infra: Noted a smaller secondary cluster (us-east-1) has spare GPUs — we could reroute select tenants to us-east if latency budget allows. Would require quick routing change.

alex_sre: Let's avoid broad cross-region moves unless necessary. Keep as option #2.

matt_oncall: I'll follow up in 20m with full handoff notes. Good job triaging.

lucy_infra: +1. Continuing to watch the queue and provisioning logs.

incident-bot: Incident closed to MONITORING at 2932110032.

matt_oncall: (follow-up) Leaving detailed runbook notes in INC-2026-GBP-782: root cause preliminary: account-level GPU hard caps + zone affinity in autoscaler. Mitigations: enable fallback pools, soft-throttling, request quota increases, add proactive alert for available-GPU < 10 in region.

anya_support: I'll start a customer follow-up thread for impacted tenants with timeline and next steps.
